title: 2602.00676v1
universal_lens: Nash equilibrium as a fixed-point operator in imperfect information games, where strategy profiles stabilize under unilateral deviation. A mathematical framework unifying imperfect information game benchmarks through Bayesian belief updates and strategic state transitions across multi-agent decision layers.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian belief updates over information sets in GuanDan using conformal prediction to bound uncertainty in opponent strategy estimates. GSI employs conformal predictive distributions over game states, enabling probabilistic inference on agent actions under uncertainty via Bayesian updating of belief nets derived from card combination hierarchies.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state transitions in GuanDan governed by subgame solving blueprints, refining policy through real-time information abstraction. GSE models dynamic state transitions using Markovian action kernels, where each primitive maps to a strategic node in a game tree with probabilistic outcomes conditioned on prior moves and incomplete information.

primitives.verbatim_quote: A Nash Equilibrium is a strategy profile σ∗where no player can improve by unilaterally changing their strategies.

primitives.name: Subgame Solving Blueprint Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: Canonical subgame solving frameworks typically consist of two distinct processes: (1) offline computation of a coarsegrained blueprint strategy on an abstraction of the full game, and (2) online, real-time search in dynamically constructed subgames to further refine the blueprint strategy.

primitives.assumptions: Game abstraction reduces complexity without loss of strategic relevance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When full game state space exceeds computational limits.

layer2.mapping: Blueprint strategy mirrors GSI’s belief propagation over information sets; refined strategy aligns with GSE’s adaptive policy update.
layer2.telemetry: Efficiency gain in policy computation vs. full game state exploration.
